description: Compute the overall electronic reaction energy of the water-gas shift reaction on Cu(111) via the associative carboxyl mechanism.
user_prompt: Compute the water-gas shift (WGS) reaction profile (CO + H2O -> CO2 + H2) on the Cu(111) FCC surface (space group Fm-3m) via the associative carboxyl mechanism. The carboxyl path consists of five elementary thermodynamic steps: (1) CO adsorption: CO(g) + * -> *CO; (2) H2O dissociation: H2O(g) + 2* -> *OH + *H; (3) carboxyl formation: *CO + *OH -> *COOH + *; (4) carboxyl decomposition: *COOH -> CO2(g) + *H; (5) H2 evolution: 2*H -> H2(g) + 2*. Report the overall electronic reaction energy delta_E_total (in eV) for CO(g) + H2O(g) -> CO2(g) + H2(g).

references: Gokhale, Dumesic & Mavrikakis, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 130, 1402 (2008)
Jurado, Morales-García, Viñes & Illas, ACS Catal. 12, 15658-15667 (2022)
method.modeling: Use a Cu(111) slab with at least 4 layers, vacuum >= 15 Angstrom, and a 3x3x1 or larger surface cell; follow the associative carboxyl path through *CO, *OH, *H, and *COOH intermediates.
method.rationale: The scored value is the net WGS reaction energy delta_E_total = E(CO2,g) + E(H2,g) - E(CO,g) - E(H2O,g), which is surface-independent when the carboxyl-cycle intermediates telescope. Jurado et al. report a PBE gas-phase reverse WGS reaction energy of +0.85 eV before empirical gas-phase energy corrections, corresponding to delta_E_total = -0.85 eV for the forward WGS reaction. Gokhale et al. define the Cu(111) carboxyl mechanism and provide the surface-step thermochemistry, but individual adsorption and elementary-step energies are not scored when delta_E_total is the final benchmark metric.
